title: Neocloud credit stress drags AI hardware lower despite TSMC's raised outlook
intro: Strong results from TSMC, ASML and Schneider Electric showed AI demand still rising, but record credit stress at CoreWeave and a report of delayed HBM4 tool orders revived doubts about how the build-out is financed. Tracked value fell about 5% between the Oct 13 and Oct 19 closes, led by servers, optics and neoclouds, while the hyperscalers and foundries held up best.
movers_note: Between the Oct 13 and Oct 19 closes all but one of the 62 names fell, led by CoreWeave (-21.5%), Dell (-20.4%), Coherent (-20.0%), Super Micro (-17.8%) and Nebius (-17.7%), while Amazon (+1.5%) was the only gainer and Foxconn (-0.2%), GlobalFoundries (-1.3%), Shin-Etsu (-1.8%) and Microsoft (-1.8%) slipped least.

items.headline: TSMC lifts 2026 growth outlook to 44% and guides Q4 sharply higher
items.summary: At its Q3 call TSMC raised its 2026 dollar revenue growth forecast to 44%, guided Q4 revenue to US$52.3-54.3B and held 2026 capex at US$60-64B, saying 2026-2028 spending will exceed the prior three years. It called advanced-packaging demand strong and said 2nm reached 8% of Q3 sales.

items.headline: CoreWeave credit stress hits a record, testing how neoclouds are financed
items.summary: CoreWeave's five-year credit default swaps reached a record 1,194.5bp and its 2031-32 notes fell to roughly 76.5-81 cents on the dollar as shares dropped. The company points to a backlog above $100B and Nvidia's backstop for unsold capacity through April 2032.

items.headline: ASML beats in Q3 and guides Q4 to EUR14.2-15.2B as customers raise forecasts
items.summary: ASML reported Q3 sales of about EUR11.7B at a 57.5% gross margin and set full-year 2026 sales at EUR44-45B. Customers raised their equipment forecasts, and management is studying EUV and DUV capacity expansion beyond 30% without committing to it.

items.headline: Anthropic tells investors Q3 revenue reached $16.8B ahead of a planned IPO
items.summary: Anthropic told investors its Q3 revenue was $16.8B and that it was profitable on an adjusted basis, with IPO marketing possible as early as the week of Nov 9.

items.headline: Schneider Electric raises 2026 targets again on surging data-center demand
items.summary: Schneider posted record Q3 revenue of EUR11.46B, up 16.9% organically, and lifted 2026 organic growth guidance to 12-14% and adjusted EBITDA growth to 18-21%. Its CEO cited triple-digit data-center demand growth in the quarter, led by China and East Asia, with US hyperscalers still supporting orders.

items.headline: SK hynix slides on a report that some HBM4 back-end tool orders may slip to 2027
items.summary: A Korean outlet reported that some second-half 2026 HBM4 back-end equipment orders could move into 2027; SK hynix did not comment and no suppliers were named. The shares extended a multi-day decline, and Micron also fell.

items.headline: Samsung and SK hynix show competing HBM4 stacks as the share race tightens
items.summary: Samsung showed a 12-high, 36GB HBM4 built on 1c DRAM, while SK hynix showed a 16-high, 48GB stack on 1b DRAM. The report cites SK hynix at about 62% of Q2 HBM shipments, with Samsung expected to pass 30%.

items.headline: Marvell adds a 3.2T retimer and second-gen 1.6T AEC DSP, and forms an OCP security group
items.summary: Marvell announced a 3.2T protocol-aware retimer and a second-generation 1.6T active electrical cable DSP for AI connectivity, and with Microsoft and Oracle launched an OCP working group on data-center hardware security.
